land_acres.label: Land area, acres (hypothetical site on the I-29 corridor)
land_acres.assumption: A round hypothetical site: room for a one-story building of the size below, truck access for grain and kegs, customer parking for a taproom, and a stormwater area. The research prints no parcel or acreage for any Fargo site and none is used. The site plan fixes the parking count.

land_per_acre.label: Land cost per acre
land_per_acre.assumption: The research holds no Fargo land sale or listing, so the study carries a round $300,000 an acre as a planning figure. An appraisal and an executed land contract replace it.

bldg_sf.label: Building, gross square feet
bldg_sf.assumption: A round size for one story holding a production hall, a cold room, a packaging and keg area, an office, and a taproom. It is a design assumption, not a market observation. The metro lease-rate figures in the research are rents, not build costs [^27].

tap_sf.label: Taproom and patio-ready customer area within the building, square feet
tap_sf.assumption: About three tenths of the building is customer space; the rest is production, storage and office. The split is a design assumption and the layout plan replaces it.

bldg_psf.label: Building hard cost per square foot, production shell with floor drains
bldg_psf.assumption: No Fargo construction cost was found in the research. The study carries a round $210 a square foot for an insulated production shell with sloped floors, drains, power for chilling and a finished taproom area, with the heavier production items priced in the equipment line. A contractor bid replaces it.

sitework.label: Site work, paving, utility taps, wastewater pre-treatment allowance and signage
sitework.assumption: An allowance for a two-and-a-half-acre site on an arterial corridor in a cold climate, including heavy water and wastewater service. No utility territory, tap fee or discharge rule was confirmed for a site; those are lender conditions.

contingency_pct.label: Hard-cost contingency
contingency_pct.assumption: Six percent of building and site work, a round allowance for a priced but unbid project.

soft.label: Design, engineering, survey, Phase I, permits, brewing licences and legal
soft.assumption: Allowance for architect and engineers, a survey and Phase I environmental assessment, city plan review and permits, federal and state brewing and retail licences, and loan-closing legal work. The research found no fee schedule, so the figure is round.

brew_equip.label: Brewing and packaging equipment: brewhouse, fermenters, bright tanks, chilling, boiler, canning line
brew_equip.assumption: Allowance for a mid-sized brewhouse with fermentation and bright tanks, glycol chilling, a boiler, a grain handling system, a keg washer and a small canning line. No vendor quote or price was found in the research. A vendor quote replaces it.

tap_ffe.label: Taproom bar, draft system, furniture, point of sale and signage
tap_ffe.assumption: Allowance for the bar, the draft lines and cooler, seating, a point-of-sale system, outdoor furniture and signage. A bid replaces it.

preopen.label: Pre-opening: hiring, training, first brews and launch
preopen.assumption: Allowance for staff paid before the doors open, test batches and the opening campaign. The research found no timeline, so the figure is round and the reserve below carries the real exposure.

working_capital.label: Working capital: grain, hops, cans and kegs inventory, and ramp reserve
working_capital.assumption: Roughly three months of Year 1 operating cost, which funds the first inventory and the gap between brewing and collecting from distributors. The research holds no days-sales figure for the market.

barrels.label: Barrels brewed and sold per year
barrels.assumption: No Fargo brewer publishes volume in the research. The study ramps a newcomer to its stabilized volume by Year 3 and adds only a modest amount after that, in a metro area with 156.3 thousand civilian labor force [^2] in a county with 126,659 covered jobs [^1]. A taproom-demand study and distributor letters should replace it.

tap_share.label: Share of barrels sold across the taproom bar
tap_share.assumption: The taproom is the higher-margin channel and the early one: a new brewery sells most of its first beer over its own bar while it signs distributors. The share falls as wholesale grows. A planning assumption.

tap_rev_bbl.label: Taproom revenue per barrel sold on premises
tap_rev_bbl.assumption: A barrel holds 31 US gallons, or 248 pints. At a round $6 a pint less about five percent for spillage, foam, samples and staff pours, a barrel returns about $1,400. The $6 pint price is an assumption; no Fargo taproom price is in the research.

whs_rev_bbl.label: Wholesale revenue per barrel, net of distributor margin
whs_rev_bbl.assumption: A round net price per barrel for beer sold in kegs and cans through a distributor, after the distributor's margin. No North Dakota distributor terms are in the research; signed distribution letters are a lender condition.

other_pct.label: Other taproom income: events, merchandise, food-truck fees, share of taproom beer sales
other_pct.assumption: A round share of taproom beer sales from private events, merchandise and fees paid by visiting food vendors. Statewide leisure and hospitality employment is 41.6 thousand [^13], but no taproom event data is in the research.

ingred_bbl.label: Grain, hops, yeast and water cost per barrel
ingred_bbl.assumption: A round recipe cost per barrel for a mixed lineup of core and seasonal beers. No ingredient price series is in the research.

pack_bbl.label: Cans, kegs, labels and cartons per wholesale barrel
pack_bbl.assumption: A round packaging cost per barrel sold wholesale (draft-only barrels use returnable kegs). No packaging price is in the research.

excise_bbl.label: Federal and state beer excise tax per barrel
excise_bbl.assumption: A round allowance for federal and North Dakota beer taxes per barrel. The rates are not in the research; the tax and trade bureau and state tax filings are a lender condition.

prod_fte.label: Production full-time equivalents: head brewer, assistant brewers, cellar and packaging
prod_fte.assumption: The study staffs a production hall of this size at a planning level, adding half a position late in the five years. No Fargo brewery publishes a staffing ratio, so the figure is a planning assumption.

prod_wage.label: Average production salary, before payroll costs
prod_wage.assumption: A round blended planning wage. The research holds the Cass County average weekly wage across all covered employment, $1,376 in the first quarter of 2026 [^1], as a general reference, not a brewing wage. A local wage survey replaces it.

tap_fte.label: Taproom full-time equivalents: bartenders, servers, shift lead
tap_fte.assumption: Part-time staff are converted to full-time equivalents. A taproom open most evenings and weekend afternoons needs a bar crew that grows with the early ramp and levels off by Year 3. A planning assumption.

tap_wage.label: Average taproom wage including tips credited to the employer, before payroll costs
tap_wage.assumption: A round blended planning wage for bar and floor staff, set against the statewide figure of 41.6 thousand leisure and hospitality jobs [^13] only as a measure of labour demand. A local wage survey replaces it.

mgmt.label: General manager, sales and bookkeeping payroll, before payroll costs
mgmt.assumption: A general manager who also runs distributor accounts, a part-time sales and events role and a bookkeeper, as one allowance. A market salary is charged even when an owner fills a role, so earnings are not inflated by unpaid owner labor.

burden.label: Payroll taxes, workers' compensation and benefits
burden.assumption: Employer payroll taxes, workers' compensation and a basic benefit package; no North Dakota figure is in the research.

inflation.label: Annual growth in wages and operating costs
inflation.assumption: A round 3% a year; no inflation series is in the research. Revenue per barrel is held flat, so the model does not assume that drinkers or distributors pay more each year.

utilities.label: Utilities: electricity, gas, water and wastewater
utilities.assumption: Allowance for a production building that chills, boils and washes all year, in a cold climate. Which providers serve the site was not confirmed, and the discharge charge depends on the wastewater rule.

insurance.label: Property, liability and liquor liability insurance
insurance.assumption: Allowance. A broker's quote replaces it.

marketing_pct.label: Marketing, events and distributor support, share of revenue
marketing_pct.assumption: A round share of revenue. The brewery enters a field with at least four breweries and distilleries in the county [^5] and has to buy its visibility.

repairs.label: Repairs, cleaning chemicals, lab testing and maintenance
repairs.assumption: One allowance for the small recurring costs of a production hall: sanitation chemicals, water and beer testing, equipment service and building upkeep.

admin.label: Licences, accounting, software, bank and card fees
admin.assumption: One allowance for the recurring administrative costs, including card processing on taproom sales.

tax_rate.label: Property tax, share of land, building and site cost
tax_rate.assumption: A planning level of about one percent of cost. The research holds no Cass County or Fargo commercial mill levy or assessment ratio, so the levy on the site cannot be computed. The actual levy is a lender condition.

reserve_pct.label: Replacement reserve, share of equipment and fixture cost per year
reserve_pct.assumption: Funds replacement of pumps, valves, taproom fixtures and packaging parts over a long cycle.

tpl_rate.label: Bank first-lien rate
tpl_rate.assumption: Prime of 7.00% on the H.15 release [^29] plus a half point for a start-up production business. No published 2026 bank terms for brewery real estate in Cass County were found; the bank sets the rate at pricing, and SBA caps the third-party spread.

tpl_amort_years.label: Bank first-lien amortization
tpl_amort_years.assumption: 20 years, a blend between a real-estate term and a shorter term for equipment. The bank may require a shorter term on special purpose property, which would raise debt service.

debenture_rate.label: 504 debenture effective rate
debenture_rate.assumption: The debenture is sold into the market and priced when it closes; the research for this case holds no pricing, so the study carries a round 6.75%, just under the bank rate. The CDC's quote at closing replaces it.

debenture_years.label: Debenture term
debenture_years.assumption: 20 years, one of the maturities the program lists. The model uses a single term for the whole debenture.

uses.label: Land, about 2.5 acres on the I-29 corridor
uses.basis: acres x assumed price per acre

uses.label: Building, about 12,000 sq ft, production shell and taproom
uses.basis: sq ft x assumed hard cost

uses.label: Site work, paving, utility taps and pre-treatment
Design, survey, Phase I, permits, licences and legal
Taproom bar, draft system and fixtures
Working capital, inventory and ramp reserve
uses.basis: about three months of Year 1 operating cost

revenue.label: Taproom beer sales
revenue.basis: barrels x share x revenue per barrel

revenue.label: Wholesale beer sales
revenue.basis: barrels x share x net price per barrel

opex.label: Management and office payroll with costs
Property, liability and liquor liability insurance
Licences, accounting, software and card fees
